IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL  NOS.  3574-3592 Of 2024
MANAGING DIRECTOR KARNATAKA 
POWER CORPORATION LIMITED & ORS.      APPELLANTS
VERSUS
K. KARIBASAMMA & ORS.                                     RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. These  appeals  are  directed  against  the  judgment  and  order
dated 11.04.2019 passed by the High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad
Bench, in several Writ Appeals1.
2. While  disposing  of  the  aforesaid  Writ  Appeals,  the  Division
Bench of the High Court observed as follows:
“18. In the above circumstances, these writ appeals succeed in
part;  the  impugned  judgment  and  order  are  modified  to  the
following effect.
a) The condition stipulating 5 years at last paragraph of the
aforesaid Resolution dated 30.06.2008 shall be treated as
being non-existent and unenforceable against the appellants
herein;
b) all the members of the land losers’ family although are
entailed to be trained in terms of the Scheme, it is only one
of  such  trained  members  who  shall  be  considered  for
employment in the normative discretion and wisdom of the
respondent KPCL regardless of consent/dissent from the rest
of the members;
c) Where the land loser’s family consists of a sole member
who is trained, he/she shall be considered for employment
straightway in terms of the Scheme.”
3. Having heard Mr. Promod Nair, learned senior counsel appearing
for the appellants and Mr. Charudatta Vijayrao Mahindrakar, learned
counsel for the respondents, we see no reason to interfere with the
1  Writ Appeal Nos.100595-10059/2015 (S-RES) C/W Writ Appeal 
Nos.100658/2015; 100677-687/2015; 100478/2015’ and 100358/2016.
1

--- Page 552 ---
impugned order.
4. The Division Bench has not mandated that one member of each
family  of  a  land  loser  has  to  be  employed;  on  the  contrary,  the
mandate  is  to  consider  a  trained  member  from  each  family  for
employment. The discretion has been left open for the appellants to
consider which of those eligible members from a land losers’ family,
who have successfully completed the training, should be considered.
5. In  such  view  of  the  matter,  we  dispose  of  these  appeals
reiterating that the claims of the respondents for employment shall be
considered strictly in terms of the observations made by the Division
Bench of the High Court, extracted supra.
6. Pending applications, if any, shall stand closed.
……………………………J.
   [DIPANKAR DATTA]
……………………………J.
[SHEEL NAGU]
NEW DELHI;
October 13, 2026

1. The petitioner-wife has filed the petition under
Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 before this
Court seeking transfer of Petition/Case No.212 of 2025
titled as “Rahul Kumar vs. Smt. Sapna”  pending before the
Family Court, Haridwar, Uttarakhand to the Patiala House
Court, Delhi. 
2. Admittedly,  petitioner’s  Transfer  Petition  (C)
No.316 of 2025 has already been allowed, transferring the
custody  petition  from  Family  Court,  Laksar,  Haridwar,
Uttarakhand to the Principal Judge, Family Courts, Patiala
House, New Delhi, Delhi. In view of the above, we allow the
present transfer petition seeking transfer of Petition/Case
No.212 of 2025 titled as  “Rahul Kumar vs. Smt. Sapna”
pending before the Family Court, Haridwar, Uttarakhand to
the Court of Patiala House Court, Delhi.

delay.

1. This Special Leave Petition is directed against the order
dated 16.09.2026 passed by Punjab and Haryana High Court, whereby
respondent no.1 was permitted to return to India and thereafter
1

--- Page 582 ---
surrender before the Court and seek regular bail. This order was
passed in the backdrop that the prayer for anticipatory bail to
respondent  no.1  already  stood  rejected  up  to  this  Court.
Thereafter, he went abroad, and meanwhile, non-bailable warrants
were issued against him.
2. While issuing notice in the Special Leave Petition, this
Court, vide order dated 06.10.2026, stayed the direction of the
High Court to the extent that respondent no.1 is permitted to
return to India and then to surrender. A further direction was
issued to respondent no.1 to show his bona fide by depositing a sum
of Rs.70 crores with the Registry of this Court.
3. The respondent no.1 has now filed an application (Crl.M.P.
No.319988/2026), inter alia, pointing out that he has already
returned to India on 29.09.2026, and that this fact was not brought
to the notice of this Court. Respondent no.1 is also stated to have
deposited a sum of Rs.50 lakhs with the Registry of Punjab and
Haryana High Court. The respondent no.1 has further stated that he
is willing to deposit Rs.10 crores with the Registry of this Court,
and the balance Rs.60 crores in five quarterly installments.
4. We have heard learned Senior Counsel for the parties. 
5. In view of the fact that respondent no.1 has already returned
to  India,  the  prayer  made  in  this  Special  Leave  Petition,
questioning the High Court’s order, whereby respondent no.1 was
permitted to return to India and surrender, has become infructuous.
6. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed of as
2

--- Page 583 ---
having become infructuous.
7. Since the High Court has granted time to respondent no.1 to
surrender till 27.10.2026, he will be at liberty to apply for
regular bail meanwhile.
8. The interim order dated 06.10.2026 stands vacated.
9. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

1. The Review Petitions in  SLP(C) No.14435/2026 and
SLP(C)  No.14163/2026 are  preferred  seeking  review  and
recall of the order dated 25.05.2026, by which the Special
Leave Petition(s) were dismissed without issuing notice to
the  other  side.  However,  subsequently  Special  Leave
Petition (C) No.14902 of 2026 and Special Leave Petition
(C) Nos.21723-21725/2026 have been entertained and notices
have been issued to the opposite parties.
2. This Court was persuaded to issue notice, as the
2

--- Page 586 ---
petitioner(s) relied upon the law laid down in  “Thota
Sridhar Reddy & Ors. vs. Mandala Ramulamma & Ors.”1 
3. Without commenting anything on the merits of the
case, we deem it appropriate to recall our order dated
25.05.2026  by  which  the  Special  Leave  Petitions  were
dismissed, particularly for the reason that since in the
two other SLPs this Court has already issued notice and all
the matters are arising out of the common order, it would
be appropriate to hear all the matters together.
4. Accordingly,  order  dated  25.05.2026  in  SLP(C)
No.14435/2026 and SLP(C) No.14163/2026 are recalled and the
Special  Leave  Petitions  are  restored  to  its  original
numbers.
5. R.P.(C)  Diary  No(s).47203/2026  and  R.P.(C)
No.10395/2026  are  disposed  of.  Pending  application(s),
including IA No. 231713/2026 shall also stand disposed of. 
6. Since, the parties are common and all the opposite
parties have already entered appearance in Special Leave
Petition (C) No.14902 of 2026 and Special Leave Petition
(C)  Nos.21723-21725/2026,  fresh  notice  in  the  SLP(C)
No.14435/2026 and SLP(C) No.14163/2026, after recall of the
earlier order dated 25.05.2026, is not necessary.
7. List all the matters together on 01.12.2026.

appearing for the Respondent Nos.2 and 3 (Prachi Kapoor and Raavi
Kapoor) respectively in SLP (Crl.) No.21381/2025. We also requested
the petitioner to ask her mother - Mrs. Sonia Kapoor to join the
proceedings  online.  Mrs.  Sonia  Kapoor  joined  the  proceedings
online, and we had a word with her also. We are of the view that it
is difficult to save the marriage. Respondent No.2 is quite firm.
She does not want to save the marriage and restore the marital
ties. 
2. In such circumstances, the only option is to dissolve the
marriage in the interest of one and all. 
3. For  this  purpose,  we  request  both  the  learned  counsel
appearing for the parties to sit, talk, and fix one lump sum amount
to  be  paid  to  the  Respondent  No.2  and  the  Respondent  No.3
respectively. 
4. We impressed upon Prachi that her expectations should not be
fanciful or something unreasonable. We also made her understand
that if we have to close this litigation, she will have to contest
the litigation before the Courts below and may not get a single
penny towards maintenance.

SYED ZAID                                          Petitioner(s)

Date : 14-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJEEV SACHDEVA
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Raavi Yogesh Venkata- 2874, AOR
                   Mr. Kotte Venkata Pawan Kumar, Adv.
                   Ms. Sahana Sathiya Narayanan, Adv.             
For Respondent(s) :  
                   Ms. Prerna Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Guntur Pramod Kumar- 2788, AOR
                   Ms. Rakshita, Adv.                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
The counter affidavit filed by the State of Andhra Pradesh
discloses that the petitioner has past antecedents.  However, the
same have not been disclosed in the special leave petition.
In the light of the law laid down by this Court in “Munnesh
vs. State of Uttar Pradesh” 1, the failure to disclose full details
of the past criminal cases registered against him is fatal to the
petitioner’s case. The special leave petition is, accordingly,
1 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1319
1

--- Page 836 ---

                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Writ Petition(s)(Criminal) No(s).404/2026
SUNIL SHRIVASTAVA & ANR.                           Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Respondent(s)
IA No. 302743/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
IA No. 302741/2026 - GRANT OF INTERIM RELIEF
 
Date : 13-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Aman Pandey, Adv.
                   Mr. Nikhil Tiwari, Adv.
                   Mr. Chanakya Sharma- 4342, AOR
                   Mr. Arpit Dwivedi, Adv.
                   Mr. Shubhendra Singh, Adv.                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Affirming the view taken by a two-Judge Bench of this Court in
Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 127/2026 ( Rutvij Bhagat Singh Wakhare
v.  The  State  of  Maharashtra  &  Ors.)  by  its  judgment  dated
24.07.2026, we reiterate that an accused has no enforceable right
to seek the clubbing or consolidation of FIRs registered against
him or her in different States merely on the ground of convenience,
or on the premise that a single investigation would be more
effective.
2. In considering such a petition, the Court must bear in mind
that where the victims are spread across different parts of the
1

--- Page 1014 ---
country, their right of access to justice, including the right to
pursue the prosecution of the accused, is of no less importance,
and must be duly balanced against the claims of the accused.
3. Bearing these principles in mind, we find no merit in this
writ petition, which is accordingly dismissed.
4. The petitioners shall, however, be at liberty to approach the
jurisdictional High Court, in accordance with law.
5. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(ARJUN BISHT)                             (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR

ITEM NO.8               COURT NO.1               SECTION X
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No(s). 29593/2026
LT COL MINAL ARUN SHINDE & ORS.                    Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Respondent(s)
(IA No. 304500/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN REFILING /  CURING
THE DEFECTS)
 
Date : 12-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) : Ms. Vibha Datta Makhija, Sr. Adv. 
Mr. Rakesh Kumar-2515, AOR
Ms. Rohini Narayanan, Adv.
Mr. Kshitij Chauhan, Adv.
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The petitioners are women officers of the Army Ordnance Corps
and Army Service Corps, belonging to the 2008 and 2009 batches, and
are presently holding the rank of Lieutenant Colonel. They seek
quashing of Paragraphs 11 and 12 of the Career Progression Policy
dated  23.11.2021  for  women  officers  post  grant  of  Permanent
Commission. Certain consequential directions have also been sought.
3. On a query, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners submits
that the petitioners have not approached the Armed Forces Tribunal
1

--- Page 1054 ---
(AFT) in view of the bar which, according to them, arises from the
judgment of this Court in Union of India & Ors. v. Air Commodore
N.K. Sharma (17038) ADM/LGL, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1673.
4. We have perused the cited judgment, particularly Paragraph 48
thereof, on the basis of which the petitioners apprehend that the
AFT may decline to entertain their challenge at the threshold.
5. In our considered view, the cited judgment does not deprive
the petitioners of their right to approach the AFT, where they may
challenge Paragraphs 11 and 12 of the Career Progression Policy
dated 23.11.2021 on such grounds as may be available to them in
law.
6. The Writ Petition is accordingly disposed of at this stage,
with liberty to the petitioners to approach the AFT. It is
clarified  that,  in  the  event  the  petitioners  file  a
petition/application, the same shall not be dismissed as not
maintainable on the strength of the decision of this Court in Air
Commodore N.K. Sharma (17038) ADM/LGL (supra). The AFT shall decide
the matter on merits and in accordance with law. 
7. We request the AFT to decide the petition/application, if so
filed, expeditiously and preferably within four months.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.
(NITIN TALREJA)                            (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR
2
